title: Samut Songkhram Culture Trip: 2-Day Temple & Heritage Plan | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 2-day, 1-night cultural itinerary for Amphawa and Mae Klong in Samut Songkhram, Thailand: riverside temples, the Rama II teak houses, and the tree-wrapped chapel at Bang Kung Camp, with opening hours, fees, and real routes.
keywords: Samut Songkhram culture trip, Rama II Memorial Park, Bang Kung Camp, Wat Bang Kung tree chapel, Mae Klong riverside temples, Amphawa itinerary
intro: Samut Songkhram is a small province packed with stories from the early Rattanakosin era: the Rama II teak houses next to Amphawa Floating Market, the Bang Kung Camp chapel that tree roots have swallowed whole, and a string of Mae Klong riverside temples you can hop between by boat. This plan keeps it easy over 2 days and 1 night, just over an hour from Bangkok, leaning into the culture and history while still leaving room for good food along the canal in the evening.
chips: 🌳 Tree-wrapped chapel at Bang Kung Camp

blocks.html: If you want a trip that mixes history with a riverside mood in one go, Samut Songkhram is the easiest answer to reach. From Bangkok it's about 70–80 km down the Rama II road, just over an hour of driving, and you're in Amphawa, the hub of this culture route. The best part is that the main sights all sit close together, so you can drive or take a boat from one to the next without long stretches in between.

This plan sets up the first day around riverside temples in Mae Klong and a visit to Bang Kung Camp, and the second day walking the Rama II teak houses before heading into Amphawa Floating Market. To make it line up perfectly, aim for a Friday–Sunday trip, because Amphawa Floating Market only opens on those days, and those are also the nights you can take a boat to see the fireflies.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Mae Klong Riverside Temples + Bang Kung Camp

blocks.html: The first day leans into merit-making and history. Start with the well-known temples in central Mae Klong, then move down to Bang Kung Camp, the highlight of the trip. The morning air isn't too hot yet, so it's more comfortable for walking and taking photos than the afternoon.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Merit-making along the Mae Klong River

items.activity: Leave Bangkok on the Rama II road; grab breakfast somewhere along the way
items.note: You'll reach central Mae Klong around 10:00

items.activity: Wat Chulamani — pay respects to Luang Pho Nueang and see the handsome teak ordination hall
items.note: An old Ayutthaya-era temple, open daily, free entry; a popular spot for making wishes

items.activity: Wat Phummarin Kudi Thong — see the antique teak golden monk's quarters, moved here from an abandoned riverside temple
items.note: On the opposite bank from Amphawa, a short drive across the bridge

items.activity: Lunch break at a riverside restaurant near Amphawa, with Mae Klong mackerel and river prawns on the menu
items.note: The short, bent-faced Mae Klong mackerel is the province's signature catch

items.activity: Bang Kung Camp + Wat Bang Kung, the highlight of the trip
items.note: A Thonburi-era naval camp and the site of the tree-wrapped chapel

items.activity: The tree-wrapped chapel — pay respects to Luang Pho Nin Mani inside an ordination hall completely enveloped by the roots of bodhi, banyan, and fig trees
items.note: The temple is open 08:00–16:30, but the tree chapel is accessible anytime; it's the image people associate with this province

items.activity: See the boxer statues and the old camp walls, and walk the shaded grounds taking photos
items.note: Inside the camp there's a wide open lawn and big trees — a cool, easy stroll

items.activity: Check in to your stay around Amphawa and rest before dinner
items.note: Pick a canalside homestay for the atmosphere

blocks.title: About Bang Kung Camp
blocks.html: The tree-wrapped chapel is where people take the most photos — the roots of four large trees creep over the whole building until you can barely see the walls. Early morning and late afternoon light gives nicer shots than the harsh midday sun. Inside sits Luang Pho Nin Mani, an old stucco Buddha image that locals here hold in deep respect.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Rama II Memorial Park + Amphawa Floating Market

blocks.html: The second day starts easy, walking through the teak houses at the Rama II Memorial Park, which sits right next to Amphawa Floating Market — you can walk between the two in just a few minutes. By late afternoon the market gets busy, so you wander and eat your way through it and finish with a firefly boat ride after dark.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: From the Rama II teak houses to the evening market

items.activity: Breakfast at your stay or a coffee shop along the Amphawa canal
items.note: This area has several canalside cafes that open early

items.activity: King Rama II Memorial Park — walk the cluster of teak houses and the museum of early Rattanakosin-era household objects
items.note: Open 08:30–16:30, closed Wednesdays; entry around 40 THB for adults, 60 THB for foreigners

items.activity: Walk the garden of plants from classical literature and the photo spots among the central-Thai-style teak houses
items.note: A shaded area with trees that appear in poetry from the Rama II era

items.activity: Lunch along the Amphawa canal — try the boat noodles and fried snacks in the market
items.note: Around midday it's still not crowded, so it's easier to walk than in the evening

items.activity: Back to the hotel for a short nap, or sit in a cafe out of the sun
items.note: The floating market really picks up from around 3 pm onward

items.activity: Walk Amphawa Floating Market, sample the canalside food, and buy some souvenirs
items.note: Open only Friday–Sunday and public holidays, roughly 10:00–20:30

items.activity: Take an evening firefly boat ride and watch the lamphu trees twinkling along the river
items.note: A private boat runs about 500–700 THB per boat, or a shared boat about 60–80 THB per person; the fireflies are clearest in the rainy season, May–Oct

items.activity: Pack up and head back to Bangkok, or stay another night if you prefer
items.note: Take the Rama II road back, same as the way in

blocks.title: Pick the right day
blocks.html: To get both the floating market and the firefly boat ride, you need to go Friday–Sunday, because Amphawa Floating Market only opens on those days. The Rama II Memorial Park is closed on Wednesdays, so avoid Wednesday if you want to see the teak houses. Planning the trip for a Saturday–Sunday works out best.

blocks.text: Riverside temples worth a stop if you have more time

blocks.html: Samut Songkhram has a row of temples lining the Mae Klong River. If you're into temple-hopping and have time to spare, you can add a few by boat or car. Each one has its own woodwork and its own story.

items.name: Wat Bang Khae Noi
items.blurb: Known for an ordination hall carved entirely from teak, telling the Buddha's life story across the wooden walls in remarkably fine detail

items.name: Wat Bang Kaphom
items.blurb: Home to a replica Buddha footprint and old stucco reliefs in the assembly hall; a quiet temple that not many people have found yet

items.name: Wat Phet Samut Worawihan
items.blurb: A temple in central Mae Klong that enshrines Luang Pho Ban Laem, a revered guardian image that locals hold in high regard

blocks.text: Getting ready for a culture trip

items: Dress modestly — for temples and the tree-wrapped chapel, wear sleeved tops and long pants or something that covers the knees; bring an umbrella for the sun too
Bring cash — the Rama II Park entry, firefly boats, and many food stalls in the floating market take cash, so carrying small notes is handy
Check the closing days — the Rama II Park is closed Wednesdays and Amphawa Floating Market opens Friday–Sunday, so plan your days to match
Rainy season is firefly season — May–Oct is when you'll see the most fireflies; pick a dark, moonless night and they show up better than on a full moon
Book your stay ahead — canalside homestays in Amphawa fill up fast on weekends, so booking early pays off

faq.q: What are the Rama II Park hours and how much is entry?
faq.a: The King Rama II Memorial Park is open 08:30–16:30 and closed on Wednesdays. Entry is around 40 THB for adults, 20 THB for children, and 60 THB for foreigners. The entrance is right next to Amphawa Floating Market, so you can walk between them in just a few minutes.

faq.q: Can you visit the tree-wrapped chapel at Bang Kung Camp anytime?
faq.a: Wat Bang Kung itself is open roughly 08:00–16:30, but the tree-wrapped chapel that enshrines Luang Pho Nin Mani can be entered anytime to pay respects. Early morning and late afternoon give the best light for photos.

faq.q: What days does Amphawa Floating Market open?
faq.a: Amphawa Floating Market opens only on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays, roughly 10:00–20:30. If you also want to take a firefly boat ride, go on one of these nights.

faq.q: How much is a firefly boat ride, and when are there the most fireflies?
faq.a: A typical private boat runs about 500–700 THB per boat, or a shared boat about 60–80 THB per person. You can arrange one at the boat piers in the market or through your accommodation. The fireflies are clearest in the rainy season, May–October, and on dark, moonless nights.

faq.q: How many days do you need for a Samut Songkhram culture trip?
faq.a: 2 days and 1 night is just right. The first day covers the riverside temples and Bang Kung Camp, and the second day the Rama II Park followed by Amphawa Floating Market in the evening. If you're really short on time you can squeeze it into a single day, but it'll feel rushed.
